They give you the keys. But nobody gives you the instruction manual.

Moving into a new home is exciting, but figuring out how everything works takes time. Suddenly, you're responsible for knowing where things are, what needs maintenance, and who to call when something breaks.

I created The Home Systems Record to help new homeowners organize those details: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

One surprising part of buying a home is realizing you're now the person who's supposed to know how everything works.

Where's the main water shutoff? Which HVAC filter fits? When was the system last serviced? These are ordinary questions that can feel overwhelming when everything is new.

If you've recently moved, start by finding the answers to those three questions. Record them somewhere easy to access so you won't have to figure them out again.

You don't have to understand every detail of your new home on day one.

Getting familiar with its systems, appliances, and maintenance needs happens gradually. The important thing is keeping track of what you learn so you don't have to rely entirely on memory.

The Home Systems Record offers 12 printable worksheets to help build that reference over time: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

Every little detail you write down about your home is one less thing to remember later.

Find an appliance model number? Save it. Learn the correct filter size? Record it. Have something repaired? Keep the service details and receipt. Those small entries gradually become a useful household reference.

Try keeping a dedicated home information folder or binder and adding one new detail whenever you learn something about your house.

Over time, a new house starts to feel like a home you understand.

You learn where things are, which systems need attention, and where to find important details. Having that information organized can make the responsibilities of homeownership feel a little more manageable.

The Home Systems Record is a printable home reference kit for that process, and a practical housewarming gift: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4596839999/home-maintenance-binder-printable-pdf

The first few months in a new home are full of little discoveries.

You figure out how the systems work, learn which appliances need attention, and slowly build a list of reliable service contacts. It's a lot to take in, but those lessons become useful knowledge over time.

If you could give one practical piece of advice to someone who just bought their first house, what would it be?
